plain_english_policy: This bill authorizes blood and saliva testing for individuals who expose law enforcement officers, firefighters, first responders, or corrections officers to contagious diseases during official duties.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment would establish a legal framework requiring exposed persons to submit to disease testing within 72 hours if court-approved. It mandates that the offender pays all testing costs and prohibits using test results against them in criminal proceedings related to the exposure incident. Additionally, it requires courts to inform positive-test individuals of available counseling and health care services.
sponsorship_supports_position: The bill's sponsors affirmatively advanced legislation protecting first responders from infectious disease exposure by enabling medical testing while safeguarding the legal rights of offenders.
evidence_quotes: This bill would authorize blood and saliva testing of any person who exposes a law enforcement officer, firefighter, first responder, or corrections officer to a contagious, infectious, and communicable disease during the course and scope of the law enforcement officer's official duties.

Any person who spits on, bites, scratches, or throws blood at... shall be required, within 72 hours of the exposure, to submit to a test designed to determine whether he or she is infected with a contagious, infectious, and communicable disease.
The state shall not use the fact that the medical test was performed on the offender under this section, or the test results, in any criminal proceeding arising out of the alleged offense.
